arw_hold_the_road.description: Kill Syndicate Footpads and Moor Adders along the road past Refuge Pointe.
arw_hold_the_road.accept_text:
I'm Commander Zel Raskal, and Refuge Pointe is a road with some tents beside it. Orgrimmar calls it a forward camp. I call it the only dry ground between the wall and Hammerfall.

The Syndicate Footpads work that road. They don't raid us. They come down off the high grass, take whatever's loose on a cart, and they're back up the slope before anyone can follow.

Walk the road and make every one of them sorry they came down. The Moor Adders lie out on the warm stones at dusk and bite whoever's walking, so kill those too.
arw_hold_the_road.turn_in_text:
That should keep the road quiet for a week or so, until the next lot comes down to find out why the last lot stopped reporting back.

I'll take a week. Out here, weeks are how I measure things.

arw_the_crags.description: Cross the High Moor to Boulder'gor Crags, north of Refuge Pointe, and kill Boulderfist Ogres and Boulderfist Brutes.
arw_the_crags.accept_text:
Boulder'gor sits in the crags north of the camp. It's the near end of an ogre problem that gets worse the further east you go, and I don't have the soldiers to deal with it, so I need to know how big it is.

Go up over the High Moor into the crags and come back with a number I can trust. Kill the Boulderfist Ogres and Boulderfist Brutes that come at you on the way. You'll get plenty of practice counting.
arw_the_crags.turn_in_text:
More than I hoped and fewer than I feared. That's the answer to every question on this moor.

There's no war band forming up there, just ogres living their lives badly. I can leave that alone for another season, and I mean to.

arw_the_pit_chief.description: Kill Gor'mok the Pit Chief at the bottom of the Boulder'gor cave.
arw_the_pit_chief.accept_text:
There's a pit in the floor of the Boulder'gor cave with a lip built round it, and the ogres fight in it. The one who's never lost calls himself the Pit Chief. Gor'mok the Pit Chief, if you want it in full.

I'd leave the crags alone for a season if I could. I can't leave him alone. Two of the bodies the kites found on the road last month had been in that pit first.

He counts out loud when he wins. My scouts have heard him from the cave mouth, and the number's far higher than the ogres in that hold. The difference is people off my road. Go down there and stop the counting.
arw_the_pit_chief.turn_in_text:
Then that's done.

I won't pretend it was strategy. There are worse things on this moor than one ogre in a hole. I sent you after the one that had our people's names in his mouth, and I'd do it again.

arw_stro_the_gate.description: Fight through the outer yard of Stromgarde Keep and kill Grevan the Gatekeeper.
arw_stro_the_gate.accept_text:
The outer gate of Stromgarde Keep hasn't opened in three years. There's a man behind it whose whole job is keeping it shut, Grevan the Gatekeeper, and somebody's still paying him.

The Antiquarian wants the keep for its history. I want it because it looks down on my road. My scouts have looked at that wall twice and come back both times with the same word, and the word was no.

So go through the gate. Every Syndicate Watchman and Syndicate Footpad in the outer yard will come for you, and once they know you can get in you won't get a second try. Clear the yard and put Grevan down.
arw_stro_the_gate.turn_in_text:
Open, after three years, and the hinges barely complained.

He had eleven keys on his belt, and four of them open doors that aren't standing any more. He was guarding a building that's mostly fallen down. I honestly don't know what to make of that.

arw_stro_the_claimant.description: Kill Lord Falconcrest in the hall of Stromgarde Keep, south-west of Refuge Pointe.
arw_stro_the_claimant.accept_text:
The man sitting in Stromgarde's hall calls himself Lord Falconcrest. He had the keep's arms carved over with his own, badly, and did the carving himself. Two others claimed that hall before him, and nobody says their names any more.

He's the one giving the orders that leave bodies on my road. Everything else in that keep is furniture.

Stromgarde is south-west of the Pointe, and you can see its towers from the road. Go and finish it.
arw_stro_the_claimant.turn_in_text:
That's the third claimant, and the third ending. Somebody will be the fourth within a month, because that keep makes the same offer to whoever walks in.

But the writs stop, the road goes quiet, and I get to stop writing letters about it. I'll take the month.

arw_wide_country.description: Walk the High Moor, the low country south-east of Refuge Pointe and the gap in Thoradin's Wall.
arw_wide_country.accept_text:
People will tell you this moor's empty. It isn't, it's just wide, and everything out there's further away than it looks. I've lost good scouts to that, people who thought they'd be back before dark.

So walk it before I send you anywhere that matters. Go up onto the High Moor to the north, then down into the low country south-east of the Pointe, then out to the gap in Thoradin's Wall in the south-west. Do it on foot. I want you to feel how long it takes.
arw_wide_country.turn_in_text:
Your legs know the moor now, and that's worth more than any map I could hand you.

The oaks are further than they look, and the wall is further than that. Remember it when the light starts going.

arw_witherbark_hollow.description: Kill Witherbark Headhunters and Witherbark Shadowcasters in Witherbark Hollow, in the far north-east.
arw_witherbark_hollow.accept_text:
There are Witherbark trolls in a fold of ground in the north-east corner, past the High Moor. They were here before any of us, and they kept to themselves for a year and a half. Now they've started coming out.

A village doesn't change its habits for nothing. I'd ask them what happened, but the last two people who tried are why I'm asking you.

Go into Witherbark Hollow far enough that they have to fight for it. Kill the Witherbark Headhunters and Witherbark Shadowcasters, and pay attention to what they defend hardest. That'll tell me what they're afraid of.
arw_witherbark_hollow.turn_in_text:
So they gave up the huts and fought you for the hollow itself, for that one patch of ground.

Whatever matters to them is down in that fold, and now I know where to look.

arw_what_veska_hears.description: Take Turned Listening Charms from the Witherbark Shadowcasters in Witherbark Hollow, and look over the deepest part of the hollow.
arw_what_veska_hears.accept_text:
Trolls bury listening charms at the edge of a camp, facing out, so they hear what's coming. Every charm in Witherbark Hollow faces in.

I want them, lifted where they lie so I can see which way each one pointed. The Witherbark Shadowcasters carry the ones that aren't buried. While you're there, get a look at the deepest part of the hollow.

Leave Harbinger Veska alone if you see her. She isn't my question. My question is why a village would spend a year listening to itself.
arw_what_veska_hears.turn_in_text:
Every one of them faces in.

They're watching something that's already in the hollow with them, and they started about when the Horde arrived on this moor. I need to think hard about whether those two things are connected.

arw_the_gap.description: Kill Syndicate Footpads at the gap in Thoradin's Wall and take the Syndicate Wall Tallies they carry.
arw_the_gap.accept_text:
I've kept this gap for a year and a half. For most of that time nothing came through it at all, and I kept a book anyway, because that was the job.

Now the Syndicate Footpads cross at night, a few at a time, and each of them carries a slip with a tally on it. Somebody on the other side of the wall is counting them across.

Bring me those slips. I've been counting on my own for eighteen months, and I'd like to see how my numbers hold up against theirs.
arw_the_gap.turn_in_text:
Their tallies match my book, every one of them.

I didn't think it would matter to me that I'd been getting it right all this time. It does, though. Thank you.

arw_what_the_kites_find.description: Kill Carrion Kites and Highland Fleshrippers on the moor around Refuge Pointe.
arw_what_the_kites_find.accept_text:
I threw axes for the Horde for eleven years, and now I keep a herd of highland stags off the road. Don't laugh at that. It's harder than it sounds.

The Carrion Kites are my trouble. A carrion bird ought to turn up after something dies. These ones have learned that the road makes bodies, so they turn up first and wait, and the stags won't graze with kites overhead.

Thin out the Carrion Kites, and the Highland Fleshrippers while you're at it. The rippers taught the kites that trick.
arw_what_the_kites_find.turn_in_text:
The herd came down to the low grass by itself this morning, the first time since spring.

People think a stag is stupid. Mine noticed the sky was clear before I did.

arw_adder_season.description: Collect Moor Adder Glands from the Moor Adders on the moor, and gather Bruiseweed, for Quartermaster Horg's antivenin.
arw_adder_season.accept_text:
I supply this camp. Orgrimmar sends me about a third of what forty soldiers need, so I make the rest myself, and antivenin comes first. The Moor Adders crawl out onto the warm road stone at dusk, and we've had four bites this month.

Bring me their glands. Pull some bruiseweed while you're out, too. It grows in the road cuttings, and you'll walk past it whether you mean to or not.

Keep the bruiseweed. I only need to see you've got it, so I know the patches are still there.
arw_adder_season.turn_in_text:
That covers the camp until the weather turns.

Nobody's died of a bite yet, because every time someone's been bitten there's been antivenin on the shelf. Keeping that shelf full is my whole job, and you've just done a week of it for me.

arw_goshek_harvest.description: Kill Syndicate Watchmen at Go'Shek Farm, south-east of Refuge Pointe, and take their Go'Shek Field Tallies.
arw_goshek_harvest.accept_text:
Name's Nalla Deeps. I came up here to watch the Syndicate for some people in Booty Bay, and the thing I keep watching is a farm.

The Syndicate took Go'Shek Farm, south-east of here, but the fields still get cut on time and the barns are still full. Somebody's farming it, and somebody's buying the grain. Bandits don't do either.

Every Syndicate Watchman guarding the harvest carries a field tally, so they know how much they're guarding. Get me some. The yield tells me the acreage, the acreage tells me how many hands it takes, and that tells me who's really working that ground.
arw_goshek_harvest.turn_in_text:
That much grain off ground that size takes far more hands than the Syndicate's got on that farm.

So the farmers never left. They're working for whoever sits in the farmhouse, same as farmers always have. I came here with the wrong question, and I'm glad I found out before I sold anyone the answer.

arw_who_buys_the_grain.description: Kill Syndicate Prowlers and Syndicate Shadowmages at Go'Shek Farm until you find a Go'Shek Grain Contract.
arw_who_buys_the_grain.accept_text:
The farm works, and the farmers stayed. That leaves the part I'm actually paid for, which is the money. A handful of bandits can't eat a season's grain, so it's going somewhere, and somebody's paying for it on paper.

The Syndicate Prowlers run the roads off the farm, and the Syndicate Shadowmages keep the house. The paperwork will be on one or the other, and my money's on the house.

Bring me one contract. I don't need the whole ledger, just the name at the bottom of a page.
arw_who_buys_the_grain.turn_in_text:
Signed and countersigned, and the buyer's mark belongs to a Hillsbrad merchant house older than the Syndicate itself.

They're buying grain at a fair price from whoever holds the farm, because grain is grain. I've been chasing a crime and found a supply chain. My clients are going to hate this report.

arw_the_overseer.description: Get into the farmhouse at Go'Shek Farm, kill Syndicate Shadowmages and take Overseer's Ledger Leaves.
arw_the_overseer.accept_text:
One more job on that farm. The overseer keeps his real books in the main house, and those are the ones that matter.

You don't need to kill him. You just need to be in that house long enough that they decide to move the paper, because a ledger in a cart is a ledger that loses pages.

The Syndicate Shadowmages keep the house. Get past them, tear some leaves out of whatever's on the desk, and leave the rest on the floor. They'll pack up within the week, and I can wait a week for the rest to fall off the back of a cart.
arw_the_overseer.turn_in_text:
Pages, and the whole house in an uproar behind you. That's lovely work.

The farmers keep farming either way. But somebody up in Alterac now has to explain a hole in the accounts, and I'm going to enjoy watching them try.

arw_stro_the_claim.description: Pass through the Lowland Oaks to Stromgarde Keep and take Forged Stromgarde Writs from the Syndicate Prowlers.
arw_stro_the_claim.accept_text:
Before you go anywhere near Stromgarde, understand what the Syndicate's claim to it is. They made it up. They were nobles of Alterac until they lost Alterac, and Stromgarde was never theirs. They walked into an empty ruin three years ago and started writing writs about it.

The writs are beautiful, and I want them. The Syndicate Prowlers carry them out to post on the walls, coming and going through the Lowland Oaks south-west of here.

A forgery that good is history in its own right. In two hundred years somebody's going to believe it, and I'd like the archive to have the originals when they do.
arw_stro_the_claim.turn_in_text:
Look at the seal work. Look at the hand! Whoever wrote these trained in a royal chancery, and that chancery doesn't exist any more.

That might be the saddest thing on this whole moor, and I'm counting the barrow.

arw_stro_the_chapel.description: Find Sister Mollis in the roofless chapel of Stromgarde Keep and bring back The Evening Office.
arw_stro_the_chapel.accept_text:
There's a chapel in Stromgarde with no roof, and someone has read the evening office in it every night for three years. The Syndicate call her Sister Mollis.

Two different scouts told me this, and I still don't know what to do with it. The Syndicate is a protection racket with good handwriting. They don't keep vigils.

I want her book. I'd take it without her if there were a way, and there won't be. Whatever she is, she's the only honest thing left in that building, and I'm sorry to be sending you.
arw_stro_the_chapel.turn_in_text:
Every evening, for three years, and the last entry is from this week.

She was keeping it for Stromgarde, and Stromgarde was dead before she was born. It'll go on the shelf beside the forgeries. They belong together.

arw_stro_the_undercroft.description: Find the stair behind Stromgarde's throne, kill the thing in the undercroft and bring back the Arathor Coffer-Seal.
arw_stro_the_undercroft.accept_text:
This is what I came to Arathi for. Stromgarde Keep, south-west of here, is a ruin with an older ruin under it. Below the throne apse there's an undercroft of marble, where everything above is plain dressed stone, and the Syndicate have lived on top of it for three years without finding the stair.

You won't find it from the hall. Go round behind the throne into the apse and listen to the floor. It sounds wrong in one place.

The Vault-Thing is what the crews call whatever waits down there. I want the coffer seal, and I want to know what Arathor thought was worth sealing. I know I'll only get one of those answers.
arw_stro_the_undercroft.turn_in_text:
Arathor's own seal, and no record anywhere of what went into the coffer.

They sealed it and chose not to write down why. Somebody three thousand years ago decided the safest record was none at all.

So I've got the seal, and I'm going to stop there. Please note that I said that. Stopping isn't something I usually do.

arc_the_refuge_road.description: Kill Boulderfist Maulers and Bound Sentinels along the Refuge Road, south-west of Hammerfall.
arc_the_refuge_road.accept_text:
I'm Keska, and I run this road. Refuge Pointe to Hammerfall and back, twice a week, on foot, because the wind riders are for officers. Nobody else has walked the whole of it this month.

It's got worse. The Boulderfist Maulers have come down off the north shelf onto the road itself, which they never did in spring. And the Bound Sentinels, the stone things that used to stand in the circles, are standing on the verges now.

I've reported it twice and been told I'm tired. Clear the road with me in mind, and then they can tell you you're tired instead.
arc_the_refuge_road.turn_in_text:
Maulers and stone ones both, and the road's a road again for a fortnight or so.

I'm writing all of it down. This time it's going in front of someone who has to read it.

arc_road_report.description: Take Keska's Road Report west to Commander Raskal at Refuge Pointe.
arc_road_report.accept_text:
There, it's written. Everything on that road, where it sits and what time of day it moves, two years of it on one page, because one page is what a commander actually reads.

I can't carry it myself. That's two days I haven't got, and the next supply run leaves in the morning.

Take it to Commander Raskal at Refuge Pointe, west along the road, and put it in her hand. Don't give it to the quartermaster. He'll file it, and it's been filed enough.
arc_road_report.turn_in_text:
Hour by hour. Two years of a runner walking the same road and paying attention.

I've had staff officers hand me less than this. Tell Keska the Pointe owes her a seat on a wind rider, and that I'll be the one arguing for it.

arc_good_growing.description: Gather Liferoot and Kingsblood in the basin below Hammerfall, and drive off the Highland Elk eating the liferoot.
arc_good_growing.accept_text:
Everyone in Hammerfall is looking at the ogres. The ogres will still be there next season. So will this basin, and it has the best growing ground I've seen since we left Mulgore, running right down the middle of it. Nobody's surveyed it, because it isn't a threat.

Liferoot grows in the wet ground along the bottom, and kingsblood up where it's dry. Pull some of each and keep them. I only want to see what the basin gives.

I'm sorry about the Highland Elk. They've found the liferoot too, and there isn't enough of it this year for both of us.
arc_good_growing.turn_in_text:
Liferoot that size, this far north, in this soil.

This basin is better ground than Hillsbrad, and nobody in this hold knows it. I'm going to tell them. They'll be looking at the ogres while I do, but I'll tell them.

arc_four_circles.description: Stand inside each of the four stone circles along the Ring Road, from west to east.
arc_four_circles.accept_text:
Look at this map. Four stone circles in the basin, and a line through all four. The line is the trunk road.

Either somebody built a road through four ancient monuments by chance, or the road is older than anyone who's ever walked it. I've been out here a year, and I'm the only one who finds that interesting.

Stand in each circle along the Ring Road, west to east, and in each one look back the way you came. You'll see it at the third. By the fourth you won't be able to stop seeing it.
arc_four_circles.turn_in_text:
You saw it. Everyone sees it at the third.

Four circles on one sightline, and the sightline's a road Arathor paved but never laid out. They inherited it. The first human empire built its highway on someone else's survey, and there's no record anywhere of whose.

arc_the_bound.description: Kill Bound Sentinels for their Sentinel Core Fragments, then stand in the easternmost stone circle, below Hammerfall.
arc_the_bound.accept_text:
The stone figures round the circles never move while you watch them, and they're never in the same place twice. The Arathor inscription calls them Bound Sentinels, and it's the only thing written by someone who knew what they were.

Each one has a core, and the core isn't the same stone as the rest of it. It's ring stone, taken from the circles. Bring me several, so I know it's no accident.

Then take the cores to the easternmost circle, below Hammerfall. The other three are quiet. That one isn't, and I want you standing in it with the cores in your hand.
arc_the_bound.turn_in_text:
Ring stone, every one. Somebody took the monuments apart to build the guards that stand round the monuments.

That's a closed loop, and I don't like it. I thought they were made to protect the rings. Now I think they were made to feed them.

arc_ask_them.description: Carry High Envoy Stillwater's parley stone to the mouth of Boulderfist Hall, far to the west, and leave it there.
arc_ask_them.accept_text:
I'm Tamka Stillwater. My people came north with the supply caravans after Thunder Bluff fell, and the Horde made me an envoy because someone had to be.

The Boulderfist are pulling down the old stone rings for wall stone. I've asked them twice to stop. If I ask a third time and they still refuse, nobody can say we didn't try, and whatever happens next will be honest.

Take this carved stone to the mouth of Boulderfist Hall, west across the basin. They won't read a letter, but anyone understands a thing with work in it. Set it down where they'll see it and walk away. Don't go in, and don't start anything.
arc_ask_them.turn_in_text:
Then it's asked, properly, three times. Anyone who says we didn't try can be shown the record.

I don't expect an answer, but I'll be watching the gate all the same.

arc_the_answer.description: Count what's left of the westernmost stone circle on the Ring Road, and kill the Boulderfist Maulers and Boulderfist Shamans around it.
arc_the_answer.accept_text:
My parley stone came back. Someone brought it to Hammerfall's gate in the night, in pieces, and left it there.

I've asked for the pieces to be kept. Before anyone does anything else, I need one thing confirmed. Go to the westernmost circle on the Ring Road, south-west of here and nearest their hall, and count how many of its stones are still standing.

If enough of it's left, this is still a conversation. If not, it stopped being one before I ever arrived. The Boulderfist Maulers and Boulderfist Shamans hold the ground round it, so you'll have to go through them to count.
arc_the_answer.turn_in_text:
So most of it's gone, and the stones that are left are the ones too big to carry.

Then there was never a conversation. I've spent a year asking politely of people who'd finished answering before I came. Thank you for counting. Go and tell the Overlord the Envoy withdraws her objection. He'll know which plan I mean.

arc_the_mere.description: Kill Mere Crawlers in the Sunken Mere, south-west of Hammerfall, and bring back intact Mere Crawler Bladders.
arc_the_mere.accept_text:
Apothecary Dellwyn Voss, of the Royal Apothecary Society, posted here to study the Sunken Mere. I've sent Undercity four reports on it. They've acknowledged receiving three.

The mere is shallow, warm and still, which is ordinary. It's also full, in a basin with almost nothing flowing into it, and the Mere Crawlers coming out of it get larger every month. That isn't ordinary at all.

Bring me their bladders, intact. They burst if you're careless, and what's inside is the whole sample. Be slow rather than brave. Bravery has cost me two couriers so far and given me no data.
arc_the_mere.turn_in_text:
Freshwater creatures with a salt gland, in a basin a long way from any sea.

Animals don't do that to themselves. Something put them in water they were never meant for, and only one thing in the last three years has moved creatures around like that. I'll be writing a fifth report.

arc_the_silt_mother.description: Wade into the middle of the Sunken Mere, kill Mere Crawlers and collect Freshwater Mere Pearls from the bed.
arc_the_silt_mother.accept_text:
The fifth report needs the middle of the mere, and that's where whatever is doing the breeding sits. My notes call her the Silt-Mother.

I don't want her killed. I want her looked at from close enough to count, which I know is a harder thing to ask of you than killing her.

While you're there, bring up pearls from the bed. Freshwater pearls, in a mere, laid out in rows. I'd like to know whether the rows mean something, or whether I've simply been alone with a pond for too long. The Mere Crawlers will object to all of this.
arc_the_silt_mother.turn_in_text:
Rows, all the way across, over a patch the size of this longhouse.

I won't speculate in writing. I'll send Undercity the pearls and the measurements, and let someone senior to me be the one who says it out loud.

arc_dry_the_brood.description: Go down to the warm gallery of Drywhisker Deeps, kill The Pick-Mother, take her Brood Shells and look over the Sump.
arc_dry_the_brood.accept_text:
I've been through the Deathguard's notes, and one line stopped me cold. The deepest gallery in Drywhisker Deeps is the warm one.

A mine gets colder as you go down. That one doesn't. Something at the bottom is giving off heat, and the kobolds have put their nursery right beside it.

Bring me shells from the brood, and take a look at the sump. A shell tells you how warm it was when it was laid, and the sump is where the heat comes from. The Pick-Mother will be between you and both. I'm sorry about that, and I'm asking anyway.
arc_dry_the_brood.turn_in_text:
Laid at blood heat, much warmer than the rock around them.

They nested down there because it was warm, and something has kept it warm since long before there were kobolds in that mine.

arc_witherbark_village.description: Kill Witherbark Berserkers and Witherbark Venomweavers in Witherbark Village, south-west of Hammerfall.
arc_witherbark_village.accept_text:
I'm Deathguard Olen, and I watch the gate. In two years, everything that's come through it has been a kobold, an ogre, or a man with a very good reason.

Since spring it's also been Witherbark trolls, plenty of them, from the village down the basin. They kept to themselves for years. Now they don't, and nobody here can tell me what changed.

I don't need the why today. Today I want fewer of them at my gate at four in the morning. Go to Witherbark Village, south-west across the Ring Road, and kill the Witherbark Berserkers and Witherbark Venomweavers. We can both be curious later, at a reasonable hour.
arc_witherbark_village.turn_in_text:
It's quieter, if not quiet.

The same thing's happening to the Witherbark in a hollow on the far side of Arathi. Sooner or later somebody will put the two reports side by side. It won't be me. I watch a gate.

arc_dry_the_shift.description: Kill Overseer Ratch and the Brine-Choked Diggers in Drywhisker Deeps, and bring back Ratch's Shift Whistle.
arc_dry_the_shift.accept_text:
I read Thugg's report and found the part he skipped. The kobold shift in Drywhisker Deeps is still being worked. There's an overseer down there, Overseer Ratch, blowing a whistle, and the diggers still come when it blows, three years into a mine that hasn't produced anything anyone wants.

I've watched a gate for two years. People don't keep at a job for no reason. They keep at it because stopping would be worse.

Bring me the whistle, and kill the Brine-Choked Diggers who answer it. I want to hold the thing they've all obeyed since before we got here. The mine is in the gorge south-east of Hammerfall.
arc_dry_the_shift.turn_in_text:
Bone, drilled through, and the mouthpiece worn a different colour.

They still came when it blew. I had your account of it before you handed me this, and I didn't believe it. They still came.

arc_the_hall.description: Go into Boulderfist Hall, far to the west, and kill Mauler Krakk, Boulderfist Hal'dun and the Boulderfist Shamans with them.
arc_the_hall.accept_text:
The Envoy has withdrawn her objection. She asked them three times, and the third answer came back to my gate in pieces.

The Boulderfist use one of the old stone circles as their outer wall, and they've been pulling the others down to thicken it. I've waited a year to deal with that properly.

I won't send the garrison. A garrison takes a hold and then has to keep holding it. You go in. Mauler Krakk first, in the long hall, because the rest of them watch him. Then Boulderfist Hal'dun, the hold chief, who won't come out from behind the ring wall for anything. Kill the Boulderfist Shamans who get in your way. The hall is west of here, at the far end of the basin.
arc_the_hall.turn_in_text:
Both of them, and well done.

The Envoy wants the stones put back now. I told her that's forty soldiers for a season, and she said she'll take forty soldiers for a season. I found I didn't have an argument. She asked three times, so I'm going to say yes.

arc_dry_below.description: Go to the very bottom of Drywhisker Deeps, kill What They Dug Into and the Deep Seeps, and bring up the Sump-Floor Offerings.
arc_dry_below.accept_text:
I've got the prospector's seam report, the Deathguard's whistle and the apothecary's shells on one table, and all of them say the same thing. The kobolds walked past ten years of iron every day to keep digging toward something under the sump. They found it, and nothing that's come out of that mine since has behaved like a kobold.

I sent people down to the sump. One came back, and he said the water isn't the bottom.

Go all the way down. Kill What They Dug Into, and the Deep Seeps that come with it. Bring up what the kobolds were leaving on the floor down there. A creature that leaves things on a floor has stopped mining.
arc_dry_below.turn_in_text:
Offerings, laid out in order. I've been avoiding that word since the Envoy used it about the pearls in the mere.

That's Drywhisker finished, but Arathi isn't. Rest and eat something. Then head east to the coast, find a bosun called Tidewright at Saltspur Landing, and tell him Hammerfall sent you.

arc_the_gorge.description: Mine Iron from the seam in Drywhisker Gorge, south-east of Hammerfall, and kill the Drywhisker Diggers working it.
arc_the_gorge.accept_text:
I'm Prospector Thugg. Drywhisker was a mine before the kobolds took it, and it's still a mine. The only difference is the kobolds dug right past the ore.

I want it reopened, and nobody will listen until I show them the seam's still there. That means samples, and samples mean the gorge.

Cut some iron off the gorge face and keep it, I only need to see the grade. The Drywhisker Diggers work the open cut and they'll come at you in a crowd. They're miners, though, not soldiers, and we're about to argue with them over a hole. I wanted that said before you go.
arc_the_gorge.turn_in_text:
That's good iron, plenty of it, and barely a spade's depth under the surface.

They walked straight past it. Every day for three years they carried spoil over a seam that would keep Hammerfall in nails for a decade, just to dig deeper. I want to know what they were digging for.

arc_dry_the_candles.description: Go into Drywhisker Deeps and kill Grubbis Tallow and the Drywhisker Tunnelers in the upper gallery.
arc_dry_the_candles.accept_text:
There's a kobold in the first gallery of Drywhisker Deeps who's never once let his candle go out, and won't let anyone else carry it. His name's Grubbis Tallow. Two different scouts told me about him, and it's the most useful thing I know about that place.

A mine run by someone that frightened of the dark is a mine with a reason. Every lamp hook and candle stub in that level goes back to him.

Take the gallery, Drywhisker Tunnelers and all, and take him. He's no danger on his own, but while he keeps that level lit, nobody below him has to explain why they won't come up.
arc_dry_the_candles.turn_in_text:
Dipped wax, every candle. He'd been dipping them his whole life.

The upper gallery was lit by his wax and nothing else. When those candles burn down, we'll find out what the second gallery's been doing in the dark.

are_the_beachhead.description: Kill Wrackline Cutters and Tidecrawlers on the shore east of Saltspur Landing at low tide.
are_the_beachhead.accept_text:
Bosun Kaz Tidewright. I'm a bosun running a shore camp, which isn't a real job. Orgrimmar sent four boats and no officer, so I took the beach and held it, and one day somebody's going to turn up and either promote me or arrest me.

Until then, the Bloodsail are on my shore. The Wrackline Cutters come along the tideline at low water, the only time the flats are ground at all, and the Tidecrawlers come up with them.

Be on the shore when they are and put them down. That way we get to keep calling this a landing and not a mistake.
are_the_beachhead.turn_in_text:
Then we hold the beach for another week.

I've written that same sentence in the log every week for two years. One of these days I'm going to get to write a different one.

are_the_ledger_keeper.description: Go into Wrackline Hold, kill Ledger-Keeper Ashkin and the Wrackline Gunners, and bring out Ashkin's Consignment Book.
are_the_ledger_keeper.accept_text:
The Bloodsail in Wrackline Hold keep books. There's a man on a dry shelf above the tideline who writes down every bolt they spend and what they spent it on, and that's the thread I want to pull.

A crew with a purser has an owner. Find the purser and you find out who owns them. The crew call him Ledger-Keeper Ashkin.

Everything they took off those wrecks went across his shelf and into his book. I want the book more than I want him, and I know I'll get both. Bring it out dry, and mind the Wrackline Gunners on the way in.
are_the_ledger_keeper.turn_in_text:
Three years of consignments, and every one goes to the same mark.

The Bloodsail aren't freelancing out here. Somebody's paying them to close this archipelago. When I send this to Orgrimmar they'll have to send an officer, so I'm about to be promoted or arrested. We'll see which.

are_mory_vane.description: Kill Captain Mory Vane and the Wrackline Bosuns holding Wrackline Hold.
are_mory_vane.accept_text:
Captain Mory Vane took Wrackline Hold from the sea side, and nobody thought it had a sea side.

The Bloodsail gave her a cave instead of a ship. She fortified it and has held the best anchorage on this archipelago for three years, with a crew nobody gave anything either. I've no quarrel with how she got there. My quarrel is the hulls lying on these flats because a lamp crew took her orders.

Go in off the shelf, not the water. She'll expect the water, she's had three years to think about it. Her Wrackline Bosuns will be with her.
are_mory_vane.turn_in_text:
Then the hold is ours, the lamps are out, and the lane is open for the first time since any of us arrived.

I've finally written a different sentence in the log. It took two years. I'm going to leave the page open on the table for a while.

are_six_wrecks.description: Look over the wrecks on the flats at low tide, and take Wreck Manifest Tins from the Wrackline Cutters picking them over.
are_six_wrecks.accept_text:
Pik Bronzewhistle, salvage and recovery. I can see wreck after wreck from here, and the tide only lets you reach them twice a day. Knowing which ones are worth the walk is my whole business, and I'd keep it to myself if I hadn't run out of days to do it in.

Every hull has a manifest tin bolted inside the stern post. The Wrackline Cutters have been prising them loose, so take them back off the Cutters, and look over the hulls while you're out there. There's one here on the shore, more out east at Bothy Rock, and one back toward Saltspur Landing.

Don't get clever with the timing. The water comes back across the Spindrift faster than you can walk.
are_six_wrecks.turn_in_text:
Tins, manifests, and most of them list the same cargo for the same buyer.

These ships were coming here on purpose. Somebody was running a route into this archipelago, and the route ate them. Before you newcomers turned up I'd have called that bad luck. Now I'm calling it a business opportunity.

are_the_hermit.description: Clear the Storm Petrel Swarms and the Reefmaw off Bothy Rock, and bring the hermit Petrel Down Bundles.
are_the_hermit.accept_text:
I was on a ferry out of Oban. Then the sea was a different sea, the ferry was on this rock, and that was three years ago. This is my rock now.

I haven't asked anyone for anything in three years, so bear with me. The Storm Petrel Swarms have taken the lee side, which was my side. I held it for two years, and then there were more of them than me.

Bring me their down, in bundles. It's for a mattress. I'm fifty-eight and I've slept on a folded sail since before any of you arrived. There's a Reefmaw in the shallows under the rock, too. I'd sleep better without it.
are_the_hermit.turn_in_text:
That's a mattress. That's an actual mattress.

Let's be clear, though. I'm not coming to your camp and I'm not being rescued. This is my rock, and I simply intend to sleep on it properly.

are_they_are_holding.description: Kill Wrackline Gunners and Wrackline Bosuns on the islands east of Saltspur Landing, and bring back their Wrackline Watch Orders.
are_they_are_holding.accept_text:
Scout Vel Ashgrave. My report to the Bosun was one sentence long, and he's read it four times. The Bloodsail on this archipelago are holding ground, and that's worse than raiding.

Raiders take what they want and leave. These ones fortified a sea cave, posted watches on the islands, and put a purser in charge of the cargo. You only do that when you want something that's already here.

The Wrackline Bosuns carry their watch orders, and the Wrackline Gunners keep close to them. Start on Gallowmast Isle, east across the flats. I want orders from different islands, so I can see whether one hand wrote them all. If it's captains making it up as they go, we wait them out. If it's one hand, there's a plan.
are_they_are_holding.turn_in_text:
One hand wrote all of them.

So there's a plan, somebody's running it from inside that cave, and whatever they want is on this archipelago. We weren't the first to turn up uninvited, it turns out. We were second.

are_gallowmast.description: Go out to Gallowmast Isle, kill the Wrackline Wrecklamps and Wrackline Cutters, and see what they've been lighting.
are_gallowmast.accept_text:
Gallowmast Isle is the furthest out, and the only one where they keep a watch on open ground instead of inside a hull. I want eyes on it before anyone goes into the Wrackline cave. Walking into a held position without knowing what's behind you is how four boats become three.

The Wrackline Wrecklamps are the part I don't like. A lamp crew on a rock in a shipping lane is there to bring ships in, and we've got wrecks all over the flats to show it works.

Get out to Gallowmast, kill the Wrecklamps and the Wrackline Cutters with them, and see what they've been lighting.
are_gallowmast.turn_in_text:
A lure, then. They've been wrecking ships onto this archipelago on purpose for three years and salvaging them at their leisure.

That answers the Bosun's question and raises a worse one. Nobody runs a wrecking operation this patient for cargo. They run it to stop anyone leaving.

are_a_hull_that_floats.description: Cut sound Driftwood off the wrecks, kill Tidecrawlers, and take Bronze Wreck Fittings back off the Wrackline Cutters stripping the hulls.
are_a_hull_that_floats.accept_text:
Oona Keelsplice, shipwright. I've spent two years looking at a beach full of broken hulls with nothing to fix them with. Hammerfall has timber and no reason to send it. We have reasons and no timber.

What I can get is what's already out there, if someone will cut it off a hull at low water without drowning. Sound driftwood, and bronze fittings off the rails and cleats. Bronze, because three years of salt hasn't touched it, and the iron's all brown stain. The Wrackline Cutters have been stripping the fittings, so take them back.

The Tidecrawlers nest in the wrecks, so clear them first. Keep the timber. I just need to see the grade before I plan a keel around it.
are_a_hull_that_floats.turn_in_text:
Not a scrap of rot. Two hulls' worth of good timber, lying on the flats where I could see it from the jetty the whole time.

Give me a crew and a tide and I'll give you a boat. A small one, but a boat that goes where you point it, which is more than this landing has had since it was a landing.

are_the_tidewrack.description: Clear the Reefmaws out of the Tidewrack, in the south-east of the flats, kill Brinemaw and bring back Barbed Teeth.
are_the_tidewrack.accept_text:
The Tidewrack is the only place on this coast with nothing built in it. No shelf, no planking, no lamps, just sand, a pearl floor and an open sump that goes down further than the cave does. It's also the only sheltered water on the whole coast, and I can't build a boat on a beach the tide takes twice a day.

Clear the Reefmaws out of it, and then Brinemaw. Everyone thinks the teeth on the tideline mean something died in there. They're wrong about that. Brinemaw grows them back.

Bring me some of the barbed ones. I need that sump clear before the weather turns, and I'm not going to be fussy about how.
are_the_tidewrack.turn_in_text:
Barbed, every one, and nothing grows a barbed tooth just to eat with.

I'm going to build a boat in there, and I'm going to try very hard not to think about what that means. Shipwrights are good at not thinking about the bottom.

are_the_barrow_door.description: Go to the door of the Drowned Barrow, north of Saltspur Landing, and put down the Barrow Shades and Arathor Revenants that come out.
are_the_barrow_door.accept_text:
I be Yelza. I watch dis barrow, an' I don't go in.

Arathor buried its eastern march in dere t'ree t'ousand years ago, an' de march still standin' its watch. Dey not cursed, dey not raised, an' far as I can tell dey not even angry. Nobody ever came to relieve dem, so dey still on duty.

De Barrow Shades an' Arathor Revenants not huntin'. Dey come out because you on de road, an' de road is deir post. Go up to de door an' stand where dey can see you, an' put down de ones dat come. Dat way I learn how far out de post reaches.
are_the_barrow_door.turn_in_text:
Two hundred paces from de door, an' not one step farther.

Dey holdin' a line, still. T'ree t'ousand years after de last person who could tell dem to stop was buried behind dem.

are_the_barrow_warden.description: Go into the Drowned Barrow, kill The Barrow Warden at the top of the stair, and put down the Arathor Revenants and Barrow Shades below it.
are_the_barrow_warden.accept_text:
You goin' in now. I already told you what dey are, an' I won't pretend dis be somet'ing else.

The Barrow Warden stand at de top of de stair, carryin' a shield dat was a door before it was a shield. It not let anybody past in t'ree t'ousand years. I stopped callin' it a hauntin'. It's a post.

De warden first. Everyt'ing below is holdin' de line de warden holds de top of, an' until dat shield come down, de Arathor Revenants an' Barrow Shades won't even see you proper. Put dem down after.
are_the_barrow_warden.turn_in_text:
De stair is open.

Marble up top, an' limestone an' standin' water below. De empire put its best people in de dry part, an' de water come up anyway, one winter at a time for t'ree t'ousand years. Nobody plan for dat. Nobody could have.

are_thane_aldric.description: Go to the bottom of the Drowned Barrow, end the watch of Thane Aldric's Shade and bring back the March-Lord's Signet.
are_thane_aldric.accept_text:
At de bottom of dat barrow, under water to de waist, facin' de door, stand de Thane of Arathor's eastern march.

He swore to hold it. De march is a drowned field wit' ogres walkin' over it now, an' de empire dat took his oath been gone t'ree t'ousand years. He still at his post because nobody wit' de right to relieve him has lived since before dere was a Horde.

Dere's no trick to dis. He won't listen to a troll who show up t'ree t'ousand years late wit' no standin'. So you go down an' end Thane Aldric's Shade's watch de only way it can be ended. Bring me his signet, so somebody, somewhere, has his name.
are_thane_aldric.turn_in_text:
His name was Aldric. Dat's his name, an' his office, an' de march it was de office of.

Everybody in dis country holdin' ground dat ain't deirs. De ogres, de Syndicate, your Horde, me. He de only one who was really from here, an' he de one dey forgot to tell. Go tell your Overlord de east is quiet. It ain't true, but it's de closest it been in t'ree t'ousand years.

are_wrack_drowned.description: Kill The Wrack-Drowned in the Tidewrack's sump, take Drowned Keepsakes from the Barrow Shades, and visit the cairn west of the Middenstone.
are_wrack_drowned.accept_text:
Dere be somet'ing standin' in de Tidewrack's sump holdin' a lantern pole. Dey call it The Wrack-Drowned.

T'ree years ago, when de water come up in de night an' de first hulls went onto de flats, people went down to de tideline wit' poles an' lamps to look for survivors. Some of dem never come back. De poles did.

Everybody who drown out dere was carryin' somet'ing, a ring, a coin, a lock of hair. De Barrow Shades pick dem up now. Bring me some, an' put dat poor t'ing in de sump to rest. Den go to de cairn west of de Middenstone. I'm goin' to put a keepsake on it for every name I can find.
are_wrack_drowned.turn_in_text:
Keepsakes, an' t'ree of dem I can put a name to.

Dey went out to look for people. Dat's all dey did wrong. Go an' rest now. Dere be one more watch on dis coast dat nobody relieved, an' it's older dan dis one by a long way.

hf_orders_for_the_yard.description: Take Overlord Gath'rok's orders to Sergeant Mok Blackstone on the muster yard.
hf_orders_for_the_yard.accept_text:
So you're the one who walked in off the Ring Road without anyone stopping you. I'm Overlord Gath'rok, and this is Hammerfall. Everything that crosses Arathi crosses in front of me, and I'd like to keep it that way.

The Boulderfist come down off the North Shelf every few weeks, find us standing in the same place, and go back up. That works because Sergeant Mok drills the garrison every day until it's boring. She's short of hands this month.

Take her these orders. She's on the muster yard, south of here. Tell her I said you'll do.
hf_orders_for_the_yard.turn_in_text:
The Overlord says you'll do, does he? He says that about everyone he hasn't watched fight yet.

Well, I'm Sergeant Mok Blackstone, and you're on my yard now. Let's find out.

hf_the_north_shelf.description: Climb onto the North Shelf, west of Hammerfall, and kill the Boulderfist Maulers coming down from it.
hf_the_north_shelf.accept_text:
Drill at dawn, the wall at noon, drill again. The Boulderfist Maulers come off the North Shelf every few weeks, and the whole idea is that they always find us standing in the same place.

This month they've been coming down more often, and in bigger groups. I want to know why before they find out we're short of soldiers.

Go up onto the North Shelf, west of the hold along the ridge, and get a look at the lip where they come down. Kill every Boulderfist Mauler you meet up there, so they know we've been.
hf_the_north_shelf.turn_in_text:
You've got blood on your boots and ogre on your axe. Good, that's the right way round.

They'll think twice before coming down that lip again. Ogres don't think twice about much, so that's something.

hf_horns_on_the_shelf.description: Take Boulderfist Signal Horns from the Boulderfist Shamans on the North Shelf and around Boulderfist Hall.
hf_horns_on_the_shelf.accept_text:
I've been listening at the wall at night. Before every raid there's a horn up on the shelf, a long low one, and then another answers from the west, from their hall.

The Boulderfist Shamans carry those horns. If they're signalling each other, then the raids are planned, and a planned raid has someone planning it.

Bring me their horns. I want to blow one myself, at the wrong time, and see who comes.
hf_horns_on_the_shelf.turn_in_text:
That's an ugly thing to put your mouth on.

I blew one off the wall last night, an hour before dawn. Half the shelf came down to the lip looking for a raid that wasn't there, and my archers were waiting. I could get used to this.

hf_the_kodo_wont_settle.description: Kill the Ring Wisps drifting along the Ring Road below Hammerfall.
hf_the_kodo_wont_settle.accept_text:
I'm Stablemaster Rukka. Kodo on the left, wolves on the right, and never the other way round. I learned that the hard way, and the kodo learned it harder.

Now my kodo won't settle at night. It's the Ring Wisps, the little lights that drift up off the stone circles along the Ring Road. They come up the bluff after dark and hang over the stables, and a kodo that's been stared at all night won't pull a cart in the morning.

Go down to the Ring Road and put out as many of those Ring Wisps as you can find. Mind the circles. The wisps are thickest there.
hf_the_kodo_wont_settle.turn_in_text:
Every one of them slept, the whole night through, and the big bull hasn't slept a full night since spring.

I'll have him pull your cart for free next time you're in the hold. Mind you, he won't know it's a favour.

hf_meat_for_the_fire.description: Hunt Highland Elk in the basin around Hammerfall and bring Innkeeper Grettha Highland Elk Haunches.
hf_meat_for_the_fire.accept_text:
We built this inn before the second watchtower, and I'll tell anyone from Orgrimmar who asks that we were right to. A garrison that eats well holds a wall well.

I'm short of meat. The Highland Elk graze the basin floor all round the hold, and a haunch off one of those does a whole table. The orcs keep telling me they'll hunt when they've got a free afternoon, and there aren't any free afternoons in Hammerfall.

Bring me haunches, as many as you can carry. I don't eat any more, but I still know a good cut, and I won't have the newcomers going hungry under my roof.
hf_meat_for_the_fire.turn_in_text:
Lovely cuts, those. You've done this before.

The fire will be going all night now. Sit near it when you're back from wherever they send you next. That's the best thing I've got to offer, and it's a good thing.

hf_the_supply_road.description: Kill Witherbark Berserkers on the Refuge Road and recover the Hammerfall Supply Bundles they've taken off the carts.
hf_the_supply_road.accept_text:
Quartermaster Urga Ironhand. These stores are good, because we've been here long enough to build shelves. But everything on them comes up the Refuge Road, and lately not all of it arrives.

The Witherbark Berserkers have started hitting the carts where the road dips past the woods. They don't take the carts, they cut the bundles loose and run, and I don't know what trolls want with salted pork and boot nails.

Go down the Refuge Road, south-west of the hold, and get my bundles back. Kill the Witherbark Berserkers carrying them. Bring me what you can, opened or not.
hf_the_supply_road.turn_in_text:
Pork, nails, lamp oil. They didn't eat any of it, they just carried it off.

Trolls don't steal what they can't use, so they're stockpiling. Olen will want to hear that. I'm putting extra guards on the next cart.

hf_ogre_iron.description: Take Boulderfist Iron Bands off the Boulderfist Maulers in the basin and bring them to Weaponsmith Krol.
hf_ogre_iron.accept_text:
This is a war forge. Not a fire with a rock next to it, a forge, with a chimney, built by someone who knew what he was doing, which was me.

What it hasn't got is iron. Thugg's still arguing about his mine, and Orgrimmar sends me scrap. But every Boulderfist Mauler on this basin wears iron bands round his arms, thick as my wrist and better forged than you'd think. The ogres took them off something, once.

Bring me those bands. I'll melt them down and turn them into something that deserves the metal.
hf_ogre_iron.turn_in_text:
That's old iron, older than the ogres wearing it, I'd say, by the look of the hammer marks.

It'll draw well. Come back in a few days and there'll be a blade on that rack with your name nowhere near it, but you'll know.

hf_the_downed_rider.description: Find where the wind rider came down on the North Shelf and take the Wind Rider Harness back from the Boulderfist Maulers.
hf_the_downed_rider.accept_text:
Wind Rider Master Dreka. The roost is full and the routes are flown, and three nights ago I lost one. A young rider, Kesh, on the run to Saltspur. Her wyvern came back alone at dawn with a cut on its flank and an empty saddle.

It came in from the west, over the North Shelf. If she went down anywhere, it's up there, and the Boulderfist Maulers on the shelf will have got to her first.

Find where she fell. And the harness, if they've taken it. It's my harness. I stitched it, and I want it back on a rider.
hf_the_downed_rider.turn_in_text:
That's her harness. The buckle's bent, and the strap's been cut, not torn.

So she got free of it. She cut herself loose before they got there. That's not much, but I'm going to hold on to it, and I'm going to send a wyvern over that shelf every morning until I know.

hf_a_parcel_for_keska.description: Take Trader Molg's parcel to Runner Keska on the Refuge Road, south-west of Hammerfall.
hf_a_parcel_for_keska.accept_text:
I'm Trader Molg, and I sell everything a soldier forgets to pack and then needs on the moor at four in the afternoon. I've made a study of it.

There's one customer who never comes in, because she never stops running. Keska carries the post between here and Refuge Pointe, on foot, and she wears through a pair of boots a month. I've had a new pair waiting for her since the last rain.

Take them down the Refuge Road to her. She'll be somewhere on the southern track, going one way or the other. Tell her they're paid for, and she can argue with me about that next time she's in.
hf_a_parcel_for_keska.turn_in_text:
New boots, and from Molg? He knows I can't pay for these.

Paid for, is it. I'll be arguing with him about that, see if I don't. Thank you for bringing them. I'll be faster in these, which means I'll be back in Hammerfall sooner to argue.

hf_by_the_measure.description: Take Venomweaver Venom Sacs from the Witherbark Venomweavers in Witherbark Village, south-west of Hammerfall.
hf_by_the_measure.accept_text:
I'm Reagent-Keeper Shelna. I keep components measured, labelled and dated, because the alternative is Apothecary Voss guessing, and he has guessed before.

The Deathguard's patrols keep coming back poisoned from Witherbark Village. The Witherbark Venomweavers coat their blades with something I haven't got a label for, and I can't make an antidote for a poison I can't name.

Bring me their venom sacs, whole, not squeezed and not punctured, or they're no use to me. I'll measure them, label them and date them, and then I'll know.
hf_by_the_measure.turn_in_text:
Six kinds of toxin, if my scales are right, and they are. The trolls blend it, which is clever of them.

I'll have an antidote on the shelf by the end of the week, labelled, dated and measured. You'll find the first one costs you nothing.
